newsitem.title: UK: UK funds watchdog plays down insurance report.
newsitem.headline: UK funds watchdog plays down insurance report.

text.p: British investments watchdog IMRO on Thursday played down a report in London's Evening Standard newspaper suggesting investment management firms may have to take out compulsory insurance against financial disasters.
Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) spokeswoman Judy Delaforce told Reuters that insurance was just one of several questions raised in a questionnaire it had prepared on risk.
"Insurance can mean many things and its just one of the things available but its too early to say what the results will be," Delaforce said.

Delaforce said IMRO had sent out the questionnaire on risks faced by the firms it regulates to a small representative sample of its members on Monday. It had to be returned by Friday of next week, she added.
